meta.disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice. Requirements vary by council. Always confirm with the issuing authority.
meta.how_to_edit: Each permit has 'triggers' (when it applies) and either 'details' (same everywhere) or 'state_details' (per state/territory). Set 'verified' to false and add a 'note' for anything you could not confirm from an official source. Leave 'renewal' as null rather than guessing. 'phase' (1–5) orders items in the new-venue timeline. Only add a 'lead_time' if it is confirmed by an official source.

1.title: Set up your business
1.hint: Start here – you need an ABN before you can register for GST.

2.title: Premises and food approvals
2.hint: Talk to your council early – many approvals depend on your premises.

3.title: Liquor
3.hint: Liquor licences can take time – apply early and check current processing times with your regulator.

4.title: Staff and insurance
4.hint: Sort these before your first shift.

5.title: Before you open
5.hint: Final checks before your doors open.

meta.default_lead_time: Check with the issuer for current processing times.

NSW.name: Find your local council (NSW Office of Local Government)

ACT.name: Access Canberra (the ACT has no local councils)

ablis.name: ABLIS – Australian Business Licence and Information Service

permits.name: Australian Business Number (ABN)
permits.summary: Your business's unique identifier, used for tax, invoices and most other registrations.

details.renewal: Does not expire – keep your details up to date

permits.name: Business name registration
permits.summary: Needed if you trade under a name that isn't your own name or your company's exact name (e.g. "The Corner Café").

details.renewal: Every 1 or 3 years (you choose when renewing)

permits.name: GST registration
permits.summary: Required once your GST turnover reaches $75,000. You must register within 21 days of going over the threshold.

details.lead_time: Register within 21 days of your GST turnover reaching $75,000.

permits.name: PAYG withholding registration
permits.summary: Register before you pay staff so you can withhold tax from their wages and report it to the ATO.

details.lead_time: Register before you start paying staff.

permits.name: Food business registration
permits.summary: Lets the food regulator know you sell food so they can inspect you. Depending on where you are, it's a one-off notification or a licence you renew.

NSW.name: Food business notification
NSW.issuer: Your local council (for businesses selling direct to customers); NSW Food Authority for wholesale
NSW.renewal: One-off notification – update it if your details change

VIC.name: Food premises registration (class 1–3) or notification (class 4)
VIC.issuer: Your local council (registering council) under the Food Act 1984
VIC.renewal: Class 1–3: every year (many councils use a 31 December expiry). Class 4: one-off notification.
VIC.lead_time: Must be registered (or notified) with council before you start trading.

QLD.name: Food business licence
QLD.issuer: Your local council under the Food Act 2006
QLD.renewal: Renewed regularly – the expiry date is set by your council (often yearly)

WA.name: Food business registration
WA.issuer: Your local government under the Food Act 2008
WA.renewal: Register once; most councils also charge an annual inspection/surveillance fee

SA.name: Food business notification
SA.issuer: Your local council (SA Health if outside a council area)
SA.renewal: One-off notification (no fee) – notify before any changes take effect
SA.lead_time: Notify your council before you start handling food.

TAS.name: Food business registration (P1–P3) or notification (P3-N, P4)
TAS.issuer: Your local council under the Food Act 2003
TAS.renewal: Registered businesses: every year (registration lasts up to 12 months)
TAS.lead_time: Must hold a certificate of registration before you start trading.

ACT.name: Food business registration
ACT.issuer: ACT Health Protection Service (via Access Canberra)
ACT.lead_time: Must be registered before you open.

NT.name: Food business registration
NT.renewal: Priority 1 and 2 businesses: every year. Priority 3: every 3 years. Renew at least 30 days before expiry.
NT.lead_time: Must be registered before you start operating.

permits.name: Liquor licence
permits.summary: Permission to sell or supply alcohol on your premises. Most states now charge an annual licence fee rather than requiring a full renewal.

NSW.renewal: Licence is ongoing; annual licence fee payable each year (for 2026 it was due 29 May)

VIC.renewal: Renew every year by 31 December (renewal notices arrive in November)

QLD.issuer: Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation (OLGR)
QLD.renewal: Annual licence fee due by 31 July each year

WA.issuer: Racing, Gaming and Liquor (Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries)
WA.renewal: Annual licence fee payable on 1 January each year

SA.renewal: Annual fee invoiced in March, due by 30 June

TAS.issuer: Liquor and Gaming Branch, Department of Treasury and Finance
TAS.renewal: Annual licence fee due by 31 March each year

ACT.renewal: Licence has no expiry; annual fee paid every 3 or 12 months

NT.renewal: Annual fee invoiced in early November, due by the first business day of February

permits.name: Workers compensation insurance
permits.summary: Compulsory insurance that covers staff if they're injured at work. Each state and territory runs its own scheme.

NSW.note: Insurer confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

VIC.note: Insurer confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

QLD.renewal: Every year – WorkCover contacts you each July. Take out a policy within 5 business days of employing someone.
QLD.lead_time: Take out a policy within 5 business days of employing someone.

WA.issuer: Approved insurers (scheme regulated by WorkCover WA)
WA.note: Regulator confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

SA.note: Scheme confirmed; registration/renewal details not confirmed from an official source.

TAS.issuer: Licensed insurers (scheme regulated by WorkSafe Tasmania)
TAS.note: Regulator confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

ACT.issuer: Approved insurers (scheme regulated by WorkSafe ACT)
ACT.note: Regulator confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

NT.issuer: Approved insurers (scheme regulated by NT WorkSafe)
NT.note: Regulator confirmed; policy renewal cycle not confirmed from an official source.

permits.name: Mobile food business registration
permits.summary: Food trucks and vans usually register in one 'home' area, then need permission to trade in each place they park.

NSW.issuer: Local council of the area you trade in
NSW.note: Councils regulate mobile vendors; renewal cycle and trading permits vary by council.

VIC.name: FoodTrader registration + statements of trade
VIC.issuer: Your principal council, via the FoodTrader portal (Department of Health)
VIC.renewal: Class 2 and 3: register every year. Lodge a free statement of trade before each place/time you trade.
VIC.lead_time: Councils advise allowing at least 14 days to register; lodge a statement of trade before each trading location.

QLD.issuer: Local council where the vehicle is based
QLD.note: Not confirmed from an official source – check with your council.

WA.note: Not confirmed from an official source – check with your local government.

SA.issuer: Council where the vehicle is normally garaged (one-off notification)
SA.renewal: One-off notification; your FBN number is recognised across SA
SA.note: Councils may also require permits to trade on public land.

TAS.note: Statewide registration through home council confirmed; renewal cycle not confirmed.

ACT.issuer: ACT Health Protection Service / Access Canberra
ACT.note: Not confirmed from an official source – check with Access Canberra.

NT.issuer: NT Health, plus council permits to trade
NT.note: Not confirmed from an official source – check with NT Health and your council.

permits.name: Outdoor dining / footpath permit
permits.summary: Permission to put tables and chairs on the footpath or other public land outside your venue.

NSW.note: Varies by council – check your council's outdoor dining policy.

VIC.note: Varies by council – check your council's footpath trading permit.

ACT.name: Outdoor dining permit (public unleased land permit)
ACT.note: If serving alcohol outdoors, sort your liquor licence first.
ACT.lead_time: Access Canberra says applications typically take up to 10 business days. If serving alcohol outdoors, get your liquor licence first.

permits.name: Signage approval
permits.summary: Some signs – A-frames on the footpath, awnings, illuminated or large shopfront signs – need council approval. Applies if you have signs.

details.issuer: Your local council (Access Canberra in the ACT)
details.note: Rules and any renewal requirements vary by council. Not confirmed from an official source.

permits.name: Live entertainment approvals
permits.summary: Live music or performances can be limited by your planning/development approval and your liquor licence conditions (e.g. hours, noise).

details.issuer: Your local council (planning) and your state liquor regulator (licence conditions)
details.note: Varies by council and licence. Not confirmed from an official source – check your development consent and licence conditions.

permits.name: Food Safety Supervisor (FSS) certificate
permits.summary: Most venues that prepare and serve unpackaged, ready-to-eat food must appoint a trained Food Safety Supervisor (national Standard 3.2.2A).

NSW.name: NSW Food Safety Supervisor certificate
NSW.issuer: NSW Food Authority (training by approved RTOs)
NSW.renewal: Every 5 years – certificates expire 5 years from issue

VIC.issuer: Registered training organisation (RTO); class 1 and 2 premises must have one
VIC.renewal: Training must have been completed within the last 5 years (Standard 3.2.2A)

QLD.issuer: Registered training organisation (RTO); notify your council within 30 days of your licence being issued
QLD.lead_time: Appoint an FSS and notify council within 30 days of your licence being issued.

WA.renewal: Training must have been completed within the last 5 years (Standard 3.2.2A)

SA.renewal: Training must have been completed within the last 5 years (Standard 3.2.2A)

TAS.note: Standard 3.2.2A applies nationally; Tasmania-specific process not confirmed.

ACT.issuer: Registered training organisation (RTO); notify ACT Health within 30 days of registration
ACT.renewal: Training more than 5 years old is out of date
ACT.lead_time: Notify ACT Health of your FSS within 30 days of registration.

NT.note: Standard 3.2.2A applies nationally; NT-specific process not confirmed.

permits.name: Food handler training
permits.summary: Staff who handle unpackaged, potentially hazardous food must be trained in food safety before they start (national Standard 3.2.2A). Keep a record of who's done it.

details.issuer: Your business (free or paid courses are available; no formal certificate required)
details.note: No renewal period found in official sources.

permits.name: Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA)
permits.summary: Everyone who sells or serves alcohol needs RSA training. Some states require it to be refreshed.

NSW.name: RSA competency card
NSW.issuer: Liquor & Gaming NSW (card via Service NSW)
NSW.renewal: Every 5 years – renew with the online refresher

QLD.renewal: Does not expire (certificates from before 2002 aren't valid). Staff must complete RSA within 30 days of starting.
QLD.lead_time: Staff must complete RSA within 30 days of starting.

WA.issuer: Registered training organisation; Racing, Gaming and Liquor rules
WA.renewal: Does not currently expire. Staff must be trained within 28 days of starting.
WA.note: Official page says courses 'currently' have no expiry – recheck periodically.
WA.lead_time: Staff must be trained within 28 days of starting.

SA.issuer: Commissioner-approved RSA providers (Consumer and Business Services)
SA.renewal: No set refresher period for RSA
SA.note: Separate venue risk-management training must be repeated at least every 2 years.

TAS.issuer: Approved RSA course providers (Liquor and Gaming Branch)
TAS.note: No refresher requirement found, but not confirmed. New staff have up to 3 months while enrolled.
TAS.lead_time: New staff can work for up to 3 months while enrolled in an approved course.

NT.note: Official sources conflict: the Liquor Act/Licensing NT say a refresher every 3 years, the current NT Government page says 5 years.

permits.name: Music licence
permits.summary: Playing recorded music (including radio or streaming) or hosting live music in a business needs a licence. One OneMusic licence covers both songs and recordings.

details.renewal: Most licences are annual and renew automatically

permits.name: Takeaway sales
permits.summary: No separate takeaway licence was found. Make sure your food business registration/notification describes takeaway sales.

details.issuer: Your food regulator (usually your local council)
details.note: Not confirmed from an official source – check with your council.

permits.name: Catering
permits.summary: Catering can change how your food business is classified (and what records you keep), so tell your food regulator if you cater.

NSW.name: Catering (and vulnerable persons licence if applicable)
NSW.issuer: Local council; NSW Food Authority if you wholesale or serve 6+ vulnerable people (e.g. aged care)
NSW.note: Requirements depend on who you cater for; renewal not confirmed.

VIC.issuer: Your registering council (confirms your food premises class)
VIC.note: Catering may affect your class – not confirmed from an official source.

QLD.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

WA.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

SA.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

TAS.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

ACT.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

NT.note: Not confirmed from an official source.
